purpose: Population census of FDA pre-notices and subsequent ClinicalTrials.gov results timing; descriptive compliance behavior, not a causal effect or trading recommendation.

design.unit: FDA notice x linked NCT ID
design.scope_rule: Primary hazard summaries include only letters classified from extracted FDA text as results_submission.
design.precision_rule: Partial registry dates are retained verbatim and concretized to the first day only for coarse date comparison.

interpretation_limits: FDA selects potentially noncompliant trials; elapsed times are not causal treatment effects.
The current registry snapshot can identify first submission/posting dates but cannot reconstruct every record field as it appeared on the notice date.
ResultsFirstPostDate includes NLM quality-control latency and is not the sponsor response clock.
FDA letters may cover multiple trials; row-level outcomes are correlated within responsible party and notice.
Recent notices are right-censored; every horizon denominator excludes rows without that much follow-up.
A registry posting is generally a compliance event, not necessarily new investable clinical information.

next_tests: Reconstruct point-in-time registry histories for a matched overdue-trial control cohort.
Estimate sponsor-level repeat response while grouping all trials in one letter.
Join issuer disclosures to measure whether post-notice registry postings contain residual information.
Treat formal Notice of Noncompliance escalation as a separate competing outcome.
kill_gates: Kill causal language until a point-in-time matched control design is implemented.
Kill a sponsor-response model if grouped out-of-sponsor validation does not beat notice-year and sponsor-class base rates.
Kill registry-posting return research if reviewed issuer disclosures consistently precede posting or announcement-purity cannot be measured.
